title: Institute of Contemporary Art San Diego Facing Financial Strain and Staffer Pushback
summary: Tension is boiling over at San Diego’s Institute of Contemporary Art due to a spate of recent firings, exhibition closures, and budgetary concerns, according to reports. title: Atlanta’s High Museum of Art Will Celebrate Centennial With Over 200 New Acquisitions
summary: This fall, Atlanta’s High Museum of Art will commemorate its centennial with the unveiling of significant recent acquisitions, some of which will be displayed in its American and African Art collection galleries. These acquisitions include a rare painting by Jacob Lawrence, a quilt by Carolyn L. Mazloomi, and a work by folk artist Grandma Moses. […]

title: Kerstin Brätsch Wins 2027 Zurich Art Prize
summary: German painter Kerstin Brätsch has been named the winner of the twentieth Zurich Art Prize. She will receive CHF130,000 ($161,000), of which CHF30,000 ($37,000) is prize money and CHF100,000 ($124,000) will go toward production costs for a solo exhibition by the artist at Zurich’s Museum Haus Konstruktiv, to open in June 2027. title: Longtime Director Stephan Jost to Depart Art Gallery of Ontario
summary: Stephan Jost, who has served as CEO and director of the Art Gallery of Ontario (AGO) in Toronto since 2016, will exit both roles at the end of the year, the museum announced. Jost did not reveal his future plans, but suggested that his departure was spurred by the early achievement of some long-term objectives. […]

title: Serpentine Announces First Participants in AI-Centric Art Tech Fellowship
summary: This week, London’s Serpentine Galleries announced the launch of a six-month fellowship program, commencing in September, that will award four artists working with artificial intelligence grants of £10,000. The inaugural cohort of the fellowship includes Reina Mun, Alice Bucknell, Alfredo Salazar-Caro and Auriea Harvey. Serpentine has long demonstrated support for artist-cum-technologists. title: Anonymous Was a Woman Names Winners of 2026 Environmental Grants
summary: Anonymous Was a Woman (AWAW) in collaboration with the New York Foundation for the Arts (NYFA) has named the 2026 recipients of funds from AWAW’s Environmental Art Grants program.
